question: Each transparent glaze passes 70% of light per crossing, and light crosses down and back. What share returns through three glazes, in per cent?
move: Losses that stack multiply, so a few thin layers can swallow most light.
ask: Where do repeated small losses stack in my work, so a few steps swallow most of the value?
trap: Subtracting 30% per glaze, as if losses simply added up.
hint: Count the crossings first, then multiply by 0.7 once for each.
steps: Three glazes, down and back, make 6 crossings.
0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49, so each glaze passes about half, both ways.
reference: Kubelka & Munk, Ein Beitrag zur Optik der Farbanstriche, Zeitschrift für technische Physik 12, 593, 1931
